A CLASSROOM WALKTHROUGH

One country. Three departments.
One year at a time.

Your teacher controls the pace. Your screen shows only your country’s department controls and the task you need to do now.

First: enter your classroom

  1. Open the class link your teacher gives you.
  2. Enter your six-digit PIN.
  3. Check the country and department at the top of your screen. Tell your teacher if they are wrong.
  4. Follow the numbered checklist on your screen. Save decisions before pressing I’m ready.

You do not need an email account. Keep your PIN to yourself.

1 · START & PLAN

What can we do with the supplies we have?

Review your resources and last year’s report. Work with the other departments in your country.

Economy

Keep food in Treasury for civilians. Allocate future funding to Military and R&D. Negotiate trades and choose affordable settlement improvements.

Military

Use delivered Military supplies to recruit or improve equipment. Save a movement or capture order for each regiment, or leave it holding position.

R&D

Choose a project. Arrange joint research before either partner pays. Fund an installment with delivered Research supplies, and choose useful city actions.

Then: save your decisions and mark ready. Your teacher moves everyone together.

2 · RESPOND, WHEN NEEDED

Our countries have met. What happens next?

Military reviews each encounter, considers alliances and chooses one opponent or holds. Mark ready to confirm the choices. Countries without required responses see a waiting message.

If there are no encounters or pending alliance offers, the class goes directly to final actions. Trade and research offers are handled during planning.

3 · RESULTS & FINAL ACTIONS

See what happened. Finish the decisions.

  1. Read any battle results: who entered, what was lost and what remains.
  2. Military chooses safe retreats where required.
  3. Countries sharing a capture agree who receives it. Everyone must choose the same country to keep the settlement.
  4. Economy enters food for every owned territory and confirms the plan. Enter zero explicitly if you cannot provide food.
  5. Mark ready once your required actions are saved.

These results are not yet the final supply totals. The teacher finalizes ownership, meals and production together.

4 · YEAR-END SUMMARY

What changed, and what do we have for next year?

  • Produced: money, food, wood and metal earned by your territories.
  • Food used: civilian meals and military meals.
  • Delivered: funding received by Military and R&D.
  • Available next year: final balances in Treasury, Military and Research.
  • Progress: discoveries, territory changes and department objectives.

Read the report and mark ready. Your teacher starts the next year. Supplies carry over once; refreshing does not award them again.

What “Saved” and “Ready” mean

Saved means the server accepted your decision. Ready tells your teacher you have finished reviewing this step. Changing your country’s decisions makes the team review and mark ready again.

If the connection drops, wait for it to reconnect. Saved decisions return after refreshing. Unsaved form entries are not submitted automatically; save them before marking ready.

Teacher setup in eight steps

  1. Sign in as the teacher.
  2. Create a class from a new world or a saved Regiment game.
  3. Assign each student a country and department and generate their PIN.
  4. Share the class link and give each student their PIN privately.
  5. Watch the roster for Working, Ready and Disconnected.
  6. Use the phase button when the class is ready. The screen lists missing decisions.
  7. Review year-end supplies before starting the next year.
  8. Download game backups. Reset a lost PIN or change an assignment from the roster.

Unassigned countries still need you to make their required decisions. Select their country and department in the teacher controls. The readiness override never bypasses missing food, retreat or target decisions.

Classroom access requires the shared service to be configured.
